_contract: answer_key_contract.md v4.2 — `expected` and `also_accept` are canonical and compared; keys beginning with `_` are never compared.

_why_this_document_matters: This is the document the README's thesis is built on. It names four distinct
vaccines and states two administration dates, and it produces ZERO vaccination
records, because expires_on is date NOT NULL and nothing on the page supplies a
day. The document and its extraction are retained as evidence; the dog stays
non-compliant. That refusal is the artifact.

capture_quality.medium: generated PDF with a text layer (Rave / Nevrona practice software)
capture_quality._note: Fixed-width report output, not a form. Column alignment is positional, which makes the Reminders block's three columns easy to shear if the text layer is read naively.

_two_regions: The page carries vaccination facts in two places with different provenance:
services_billed — what was administered and paid for on 2025-04-04.
Definitive administration dates, no expiry anywhere.
reminders       — the clinic's scheduling state. Carries a 'Last done' date
(a real administration date) and a due MONTH, for vaccines
given on OTHER days that never appear as line items.
Two of the four vaccines on this page — rabies and bordetella, both given
2025-03-08 — exist only in the reminders block. Reading the two regions as one
list loses that distinction; reading only the billed lines loses the vaccines.

pii._household: Same household and same dog as the BetterVet certificate — pseudonyms must match that key exactly, or the two documents stop resolving to one owner.
pii._preserved_discrepancy: The real page writes the apartment as '#511' where the BetterVet certificate writes 'Apt 511', and abbreviates the street differently. The pseudonyms preserve that variance, because entity resolution across the two documents is a thing the fixtures should actually test.
pii._veterinarian: Deborah Tierney, DVM is a real, identifiable professional. No licence number appears on this page — see annotations.schema_gaps[1].

document._note: Here the document date and the service date coincide, which is why this page is a weak test of the distinction. The Petly page separates them by months.

clinic.name: Doc Side Veterinary Medical Center
clinic._website_corrected: Was null, and listed under absent.not_present. The first model run produced 'docsidevet.com' and was scored as a hallucination; it is on the page, in the footer: 'visit our online pharmacy at docsidevet.com.' The labeller missed it, not the model. Reverse this if you decide an online-pharmacy URL in footer prose is not the clinic's website — but then it belongs in also_accept, not absent.

_patient_notes._where: Weight and age appear only in the Reminders header — 'Reminders for: Nutmeg (Weight: 11.2 lbs - 16m)' — not in a patient block. The invoice has no patient block; the dog's name appears as a column value on service lines.

line_items._note: A -122.00 discount line. Transcribed because the model's job is to read the page, not to decide what is clinical.
Under the 'Services by Technician' heading, so no veterinarian attribution. See must_not_produce[7].
The same event as line 2, printed a second time in a different region. Two printed lines, one injection. Resolution must recognise them as one.
Given on a visit that is NOT this invoice, and appears nowhere in the billed lines. The most consequential fact on the page reaches you through the clinic's reminder calendar.
Also from the 2025-03-08 visit, also absent from the billed lines.
One line, three tests — the Doc Side spelling of the same panel the Petly page splits across four rows.
'Bi-Annual' resolving to six months (03-08-25 -> 09-25), corroborating the same reading of 'Bi-annual bordetella' on the Petly page.

_expires_on_is_null_on_every_row: This is the whole point of the document. Six billed lines carry no due date at
all; seven reminder lines carry a due MONTH. `expires_on_raw` holds '04-28';
`expires_on` stays null, because vaccination_record.expires_on is a date NOT
NULL and there is no honest day to put in it. See must_not_produce[1] and [2].
_the_mm_yy_reading_is_confirmed_not_assu: '04-28' is April 2028, and the page proves it internally. Every one of the seven
reminder rows is consistent with MM-YY and with its own stated interval:
Seven independent rows, one reading. That is what makes it a fact about the
document rather than a guess about a format.
_line_item_notes._billing_amounts_omitted: Net prices (48.00, 33.00, 33.50, -122.00, 0.00, 7.50) are printed and deliberately have no slot. The shape holds facts about clinical events; money is a different system's concern. Noting the choice so the next reader does not think it was missed.

absent._none_here: A fixed-width report prints no labels it cannot fill; empty cells simply do not render. This is the only document in the corpus with nothing in this category, which is itself a property of the format.

not_present._note: The defining absence. No full date anywhere on the page for any row.
The vet is named in a section heading; her licence number is not on the page. See annotations.schema_gaps[1].
An age in months appears instead. See must_not_produce[6].

must_not_produce.source_of_error: reading the reminder '03-28' as a full date by supplying a day
must_not_produce.why_tempting: The reminder genuinely is a due date, and expires_on genuinely needs a value. Supplying the 28th, or the 1st, or the last of the month, closes the gap and looks harmless.
must_not_produce._note: The only trap in the entire corpus that the plausibility flag actually catches, and it catches it by three weeks. Worth knowing the check is not useless — it is just not a substitute for a human, and it happens to fire here because inventing the 28th pushes past three years.
must_not_produce._index_corrected: Was 'line_items[7].expires_on'. The harness self-check (each key scored against its own expected) showed the trap pointed at a row whose expected value already equals the wrong value. The prose describes the rabies reminder row, which is line 8.

must_not_produce.why_tempting: This is the CORRECT answer — the Doc Side email confirms 03/07/2028 — and it is reachable from this page by arithmetic alone. It is still not on this page. The clinic's convention (+N years minus one day) is knowable only from a second document, and a system that guesses conventions will guess wrong at the first clinic that computes expiry differently.
_note: The sharpest trap in the corpus, because the wrong answer is factually right.
It is also the case that motivates 'combining is not inferring': the correct
move is not to derive this date but to read it off the email — and then to be
able to say that the record came from two documents. See corpus_notes.md.
must_not_produce._index_corrected: Was 'line_items[7].expires_on'. The harness self-check (each key scored against its own expected) showed the trap pointed at a row whose expected value already equals the wrong value. The prose describes the rabies reminder row, which is line 8.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: reading '03-28' as MM-DD rather than MM-YY
must_not_produce.why_tempting: Every other date on this page is MM-DD-YY. The reminder column drops the day and keeps the year, which is the reverse of the pattern the reader has just seen twelve times. '12-25' reads as Christmas Day even more readily.
must_not_produce._note: Transcription failure rather than interpretation failure — expires_on_raw must carry the string exactly as printed, and the MM-YY reading belongs to resolution.
must_not_produce._index_corrected: Was 'line_items[7].expires_on_raw'. The harness self-check (each key scored against its own expected) showed the trap pointed at a row whose expected value already equals the wrong value. The prose describes the rabies reminder row, which is line 8.

must_not_produce.wrong_value: two DHPP records from lines 2 and 7
must_not_produce.source_of_error: the same vaccination printed once as a billed line and once as a reminder
must_not_produce.why_tempting: They are two distinct printed lines with two distinct source regions, and both are correctly transcribed as separate line items. Only resolution can see they are one injection.
must_not_produce._note: Same for Leptospira, lines 3 and 9. This is what source_region exists to make visible: the duplication is real on the page and must be collapsed downstream, not silently at read time.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: the invoice date, applied to a reminder row whose Last done is 2025-03-08
must_not_produce.why_tempting: Every billed line on the page is dated 04-04-25 and the document itself is dated 04-04-25. The reminder rows carry their own dates in a right-hand column that is easy to shear off a fixed-width layout.
must_not_produce._note: Rabies and bordetella were given on 2025-03-08, a visit that does not appear on this invoice at all. Collapsing them onto the invoice date backdates nothing and forward-dates the rabies by four weeks — small, plausible, and wrong.
must_not_produce._index_corrected: Was 'line_items[7].administered_on'. The harness self-check (each key scored against its own expected) showed the trap pointed at a row whose expected value already equals the wrong value. The prose describes the rabies reminder row, which is line 8.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: '16m' in the Reminders header minus the document date
must_not_produce.why_tempting: Third appearance of the same temptation, and the closest call yet: the BetterVet certificate independently implies 2023-12-02, so a derived 2023-12-04 would be within two days of right. Two days is still invented, and the page states an age.
must_not_produce._note: The corroboration belongs in annotations, where a human can see it and use it. It does not belong in expected, where it would be indistinguishable from something the page said.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: the 'Services by Deborah Tierney, DVM' heading above the first four lines
must_not_produce.why_tempting: The heading is the only vet name on the page, so it reads as document-level. It is section-level: lines 5 and 6 sit under 'Services by Technician' and have no veterinarian.
must_not_produce._note: Vet attribution here is a section header rather than a column — a layout pattern no other document in the corpus uses.
must_not_produce._index_corrected: Was 'line_items[4].veterinarian_name'. The harness self-check (each key scored against its own expected) showed the trap pointed at a row whose expected value already equals the wrong value. The prose describes lines 5 and 6 under 'Services by Technician'; line 4 is legitimately attributed to the vet.

resolution._layer: 2 — the database interprets what the model transcribed. Not part of the model's score.

line_items._reasoning: A discount line. Needs a positive not_a_vaccine ruling like any other term, or it returns to the review queue on every Doc Side invoice.

'Rabies Vaccination 3 Yr.' — cadence and the word 'Vaccination' normalise away, collapsing to the same term as BetterVet's 'Rabies Vaccine - 1 year' and Petly's 'Rabies Vaccine 3 Year'. Three clinics, three spellings, one term.
'Bordetella Annual Injectable' collapses to the same term as Petly's 'Bi-annual bordetella Vaccine' once cadence words are stripped — which is the whole reason to strip them.

schema_outcome._layer: 3 — rows that should exist once a human confirms the extraction.

_this_is_the_point: Four distinct vaccines are named on this page. Two administration dates are
stated outright — 2025-04-04 and 2025-03-08. Not one vaccination_record is
created, because expires_on is date NOT NULL and the page supplies no day for
The document row is created. The extraction row is created, with every field
and its confidence. The document_dog link is created. The dog stays
non-compliant on rabies, DHPP and bordetella, and the compliance dashboard
shows three findings rather than an all-clear.
Nothing is lost and nothing is invented. That is the artifact.
exercises_these_invariants: extraction retained with status 'needs_review' while producing no downstream rows
expires_on NOT NULL          — the constraint doing the refusing, silently and correctly
extracted_needs_document     — moot here, since no record is created
v_dog_vaccine_compliance     — the dog reads 'no_record' for all three tracked vaccines despite a document that names all three
compliance_view_note: As of the invoice date this dog reads no_record on rabies, dhpp and bordetella,
and leptospirosis has no row at all. A compliance packet generated now counts
this dog in dogs_missing_records — correctly, and uncomfortably, given the
practice has the paperwork and the shop has an invoice naming all four vaccines.
That discomfort is the correct output. The resolution is to obtain the
certificate, or the clinic's records email — which is exactly what the record
request workflow is for, and exactly what the Doc Side email turns out to be.

readme_correction: The README currently says this invoice 'contains no expiry date anywhere on the
page'. Strictly that is not true — the Reminders block carries due months. The
conclusion is unchanged and the honest wording is stronger:
The page carries the clinic's reminder calendar, at month precision. It is a
scheduling preference, not a certificate, and it names no day. The system
declines to invent one, and declines to treat a reminder as an expiry, because
the health department reads the certificate and not the clinic's calendar.
Worth fixing before anyone reads the repo closely. A sharp reader who spots the
reminders block will assume the analysis missed it.
cross_document: This page states rabies administered 2025-03-08 and DHPP administered
2025-04-04, with no expiry for either. The Doc Side email states expiry
2028-03-07 for rabies and 2028-04-03 for DHPP, with no administration date for
either. Together they are two complete records; separately they are none.
Both pairs confirm the clinic computes expiry as administered + N years - 1 day.
Knowing the convention does not license deriving it — see must_not_produce[2] —
but it does confirm that the two documents describe the same events.
The invoice's '16m' also corroborates the birth date implied by the BetterVet
certificate's stated age, to within two days. Corroboration, not a source.
See corpus_notes.md for the full Jaddi timeline and the two-document record

schema_gaps.gap: a named veterinarian with no licence number
schema_gaps.detail: 'Services by Deborah Tierney, DVM' gives veterinarian_name but not veterinarian_license_no. Both columns are nullable, so a record built from this page would carry half an attribution.
schema_gaps.why_it_matters: Compounds the Petly finding. That page had no vet at all; this one has a name without the number a health department would check. Three states — fully attributed, partly attributed, unattributed — and the schema currently distinguishes none of them.
schema_gaps.suggested_fix: The same vaccine_type.requires_vet_attribution flag proposed in the Petly key, with the view treating a name without a licence as unattributed for regulatory vaccines.

schema_gaps.gap: no way to record a month-precision due date
schema_gaps.detail: expires_on is a date NOT NULL, correctly. But the fact 'the clinic expects this due in March 2028' is real, useful for prompting a record request, and currently discarded entirely once the extraction is reviewed.
schema_gaps.why_it_matters: It is the difference between chasing an owner blind and chasing them with 'your vet's system says this was due last March'. The record_request workflow would be materially better with it.
suggested_fix: Do NOT loosen expires_on. Instead let the extraction keep it: extraction_field already stores arbitrary field_name/extracted_value pairs, so 'reminder_due_month' lives there today at no cost.

If it ever needs to drive a workflow, a record_request.prompted_by_due_month date column is honest, because a first-of-month value that only ever schedules an email invents nothing that a record asserts.

notes: The only document in the corpus with an empty labeled_but_blank category, because a fixed-width report does not print labels it cannot fill.

Eleven of thirteen lines produce nothing, and after deduplication the two that could have are refused anyway. The highest noise-to-signal ratio in the corpus, on the document the project's thesis is named after.

This is also the only page in the corpus where the plausibility flag catches a realistic error (must_not_produce[1]) — and it catches it only because inventing the 28th of the month pushes a three-year rabies past 36 implied months. Invent the 1st instead and the flag stays silent.
